architecture.decision: Option B from the recon: a dependency-free node:http server in a NEW src/editor/ module on its OWN 127.0.0.1 origin, launched by a tsx CLI (src/cli-editor.ts), serving one hand-written HTML page + one CSS + one vanilla-JS asset, with EVERY decision behind a typed JSON API.
architecture.whyOwnOrigin: The preview bridge's security model is cross-origin BY CONSTRUCTION: it posts only to explicitly allowlisted origins (never "*") and accepts only messages whose event.origin is allowlisted AND whose event.source is the embedder. Serving the editor from the preview's own origin makes both guards vacuous. Two ports, two origins, one postMessage channel — and 28.P4.44 proves an un-allowlisted origin receives nothing and cannot command the bridge.

rejected.option: A second Next.js app under src/
rejected.why: next dev/build REWRITES the SHARED root tsconfig.json on first run (it injects jsx/plugins/include/exclude) and drops .next/types/*.ts inside src/, which `tsc --noEmit` over src/**/*.ts would then typecheck — breaking the typecheck gate for every other Task-28 agent running concurrently. Measured precondition: the repo root has no next.config, no app/ or pages/ dir, and the root tsconfig has no "jsx" option and includes only src/**/*.ts + scripts/**/*.ts.

rejected.option: A static HTML file opened over file://
rejected.why: the bridge's inbound guard is `if (origins.indexOf(event.origin) === -1) return;` and a file:// document posts origin "null". Making it work requires weakening the exact security property Phase 3 was measured on.

rejected.option: Serving the editor from the authoring proxy at a reserved path
rejected.why: same-origin with the preview: both inbound guards become vacuous, and editor bytes move inside the serve boundary whose separation from the production bake is the tested property.

rejected.option: Any new dependency (Vite, a component library, a bundler)
rejected.why: no network budget by contract. Built on next/react/playwright/parse5/zod/pino/tsx only — and the editor itself uses none of them except playwright in its test.

appLocation.separateFromProductionOutput: the editor never writes into a generated customer application. It reads the IMMUTABLE Recon Template run and writes only (a) release-project.json + revisions/ through src/release, and (b) the authoring preview's own overlay files. The production bake copies the immutable template run, so no editor byte can reach a package — re-proven this phase by scripts/smoke-authoring-preview.ts 28.P3.34/35/36 (real production package, 0 occurrences of the bridge marker, 0 of the authoring patch) after the bridge was extended.
appLocation.installedDepsOnly: node:http + node:net, exactly like src/authoring-preview/serve.ts, src/theme/serve.ts, src/seo/serve.ts and src/assets/serve.ts already do.

architecture.layoutShipped: top bar (Site select · Page select · Desktop/Mobile · Preview/QA · Select-mode · status · Undo) / left rail (Pages, Regions) / centre (the real preview in an iframe, or the QA report) / right (Inspector tabs: Slot · Region · Theme · Logo).
architecture.clientIsThin: The browser asset is deliberately wiring only — iframe plumbing, postMessage, one <style> rewrite inside the preview, and form rendering from server-provided data. `tsc --noEmit` covers src/**/*.ts and a browser asset is outside the type system either way, so slot inversion, inspector assembly, group composition, theme validation, enablement, revisions and the AI-rewrite contract are ALL server-side and typechecked. The 2.9 MB slot-bindings file is never sent to the browser.

DOM identity is the EXISTING data-wr-node / data-wr-dyn-node plus the slot-bindings.json inversion. 28.P4.45 measures 0 elements carrying data-wr-slot in the live preview and 0 occurrences of the string in the served HTML.

triggerRecovery.where: src/authoring-preview/bridge.ts recoverTrigger() — in-page, because report.node is ALWAYS null on a mounted dynamic-template element

domToSlotInversion.textIndexRule: NOT used by the editor at all, and that is the point: the editor never addresses a text segment itself. It writes authored.slotValues[slotKey] and the template's OWN applier (with its expectedValue guard) rewrites every bound occurrence. The recon's `childNodes.filter(n => n.nodeType !== 8)[childIndex]` finding therefore stays inside the runtime, where it already is.

hoverOverlay.technique: ONE <style data-wr-editor-style="1"> appended to <head>, textContent rewritten per hover to `[data-wr-viewport="<vp>"] [data-wr-node="<n>"]{outline:2px solid #0a84ff !important;outline-offset:-1px !important;}` (and #f0a000 for the selected element). It targets the EXISTING attribute, so ZERO attributes are set on any customer element and ZERO nodes are inserted into the customer subtree.
hoverOverlay.whyOutline: outline is painted outside the border box and never participates in layout, so unlike a border/box-shadow/inserted box it cannot move anything, and unlike an absolutely-positioned box it cannot extend the scrollable overflow area.
hoverOverlay.roleTypeIndicator: drawn in the EDITOR document (a fixed badge positioned from the reported rect), never inside the customer page — zero geometry cost by construction. It follows iframe scrolling because the bridge now emits geometry ticks.

measuredGeometryDelta.method: getBoundingClientRect{x,y,width,height} for EVERY element in the preview document plus 6 document metrics (documentElement.scrollWidth/scrollHeight/clientWidth/clientHeight, body.scrollWidth/scrollHeight); the injected <style> is filtered out of both snapshots; max absolute delta over ~32,000 numbers
measuredGeometryDelta.noiseFloor: 0 (baseline vs baseline, 400 ms apart, 8,010 elements) — so a nonzero result would be real
measuredGeometryDelta.desktop1440x900: max delta EXACTLY 0 over 13 probes, one per tag kind (main, section, nav, div, ul, li, p, h1, h2, a, span, button, img), 8,010 elements + 6 document metrics
measuredGeometryDelta.mobile390x844: max delta EXACTLY 0 over the same 13 probe kinds
measuredGeometryDelta.probeDesignIsMeasured: the FIRST version of this check hovered one inline anchor and read 0 even when the highlight was deliberately changed from `outline` to `border` — the template's boxes are border-box, so a border on a childless inline element moves nothing. The check was strengthened to one probe per tag kind, and re-injecting the same break then produced a 4.0001220703125 px delta at section#n000004 on desktop and 4 px on mobile. The zero above is therefore a measurement with a demonstrated ability to fail.

revisionAndUndo.transactionBoundary: a keystroke calls POST /api/preview-value (debounced 250 ms), which writes the preview overlay ONLY — no project write, no revision. An explicit Save calls commitAuthoredEdits(), which appends exactly one revision, and none at all when nothing moved.
measured: 7 keystrokes produced 0 revisions while the typed value WAS already served by the preview and was NOT in the project's authoritative authored state (28.P4.38)
the single Save that followed appended exactly 1 revision (28.P4.39)
re-saving the identical value wrote nothing and appended no revision (28.P4.41)
revisionAndUndo.undo: restoreAuthoredRevision APPENDS the earlier snapshot as a new head. 28.P4.42 asserts the chain grew by exactly one, the new head's origin is "restore", its restoredFrom is the target revisionId, its authoredStateHash equals the target's, and every pre-existing revision record is byte-identical afterwards. 28.P4.43 asserts the undone value is actually gone from the authoritative authored state.
revisionAndUndo.themeCommitNote: AuthoredEdit has no set-theme op today, so src/editor/commit.ts composes the new AuthoredState and hands it to the SAME commitAuthoredState, re-deriving the no-op guard from hashAuthoredState (the identical canonicalisation appendAuthoredRevisionIfChanged compares on). See integrationSeams.

aiRewriteContract.noCredentials: There is no LLM API key in this repo (src/config/env.ts declares only FIRECRAWL_API_KEY) and no vendor SDK was added. The feature runs on the EXISTING provider-neutral ContentGenerator seam and works with --provider fake (FakeContentGenerator, deterministic and offline) or provider "result" (loadManualGenerationResult — an operator-authored generation-result.json, parsed by the same schema and the same validator).
aiRewriteContract.endpoint: POST /api/ai-rewrite { scope: {kind:"slot"|"region", slotKey?|regionId?}, route, provider, resultFile? }
aiRewriteContract.requestContext: customer brief (the content run's intent.json verbatim, else the project's intent.rawIntent — and a REFUSAL, not an invented brief, when neither exists) + the SiteContentPlan from the content run's generation-result.json + the route + the selected PageRegion (regionId, landmark, rootTag, slotCount) + the contained Content Units built by buildContentUnits() + each unit slot's recorded constraints + CONTENT_POLICY (content-policy-v1) + the run's own generation instructions.
aiRewriteContract.responseContract: KEYED STRUCTURED SLOT VALUES. `proposed` is slotKey → value; any key the provider returns that is not in the requested scope is listed in `outOfScope` and REFUSED — never split, truncated or reassigned. `unresolved` entries stay unresolved and are NOT filled in. Nothing is applied by the call: the operator applies the proposal through the ordinary Save path, so an AI rewrite creates exactly one revision like any other edit.
aiRewriteContract.measured: 28.P4.48 (the request really carries brief + sitePlan + units + slot constraints + policy id + instructions), 28.P4.49 (every proposed key is in scope, every value is a string, outOfScope is empty, and the revision count is unchanged by the call), 28.P4.50 (a PageRegion rewrite is scoped by that region's own slot keys).
aiRewriteContract.includeReviewNote: a hand-picked rewrite sets includeReview:true, because the operator selected that exact slot/region. This loosens no batch gate — review slots stay excluded from batch content runs — and it records nothing about human approval.

regionEnablement.port: src/editor/panels.ts RegionEnablementPort — read(site, regionIds) / write(site, regionId, enabled); startVisualEditor({ regionEnablement }) takes any implementation
regionEnablement.statusInThisBuild: WIRED. The enablement builder landed src/release/enablement.ts (loadEnablementInputs / evaluateRegionDisable / evaluateRouteDisable / resolveEnablement) and the disable-region / enable-region AuthoredEdit ops while this editor was being written, so src/editor/region-enablement.ts calls them directly: evaluateRegionDisable for the decision, commitAuthoredEdits to record it, resolveEnablement to report the current state.
regionEnablement.honestyRule: a region whose recorded disable is REFUSED by the resolver reports enabled:null (UNKNOWN) with the refusal text verbatim — never 'disabled', because a recorded decision the bake will not apply is not an off switch. A refusal (code, message, affected routes, cascade) is surfaced verbatim and never softened.
regionEnablement.fallback: UNWIRED_REGION_ENABLEMENT is still exported and still reports enabled:null / editable:false, and POST /api/region-enablement answers 501 with REGION_ENABLEMENT_SEAM when a port reports wired:false. If the integration agent needs a different API shape, substituting the port is the whole change.
regionEnablement.notWiredHere: ROUTE disable. evaluateRouteDisable exists and the Pages rail is the obvious place for it, but this phase shipped no route toggle — the Pages list is navigation only. That is a gap, not a claim.

integrationSeams.authoredEditSetTheme: REQUESTED SEAM: `AuthoredEdit` covers slot values, assets, brand decisions and enablement, but not the theme block. src/editor/commit.ts commitThemeTokens() composes the state itself and commits through commitAuthoredState. If src/release adds `{op:"set-theme-token"|"clear-theme-token"}`, commitThemeTokens collapses into commitEdits with no caller change.

performance.readingTheEditLatencies: text/url/theme 'visible in the browser' (~0.83–0.91 s median) is the FULL operator-visible path and includes the editor's own 250 ms debounce plus a complete iframe document re-fetch. The gap is UI policy (debounce + full reload), not engine cost, and could be closed later by re-rendering without a document reload; it is reported rather than tuned away.

limitations: The browser-side asset is NOT covered by `tsc --noEmit` (include is src/**/*.ts and the client is a TS-emitted string). It is kept to wiring on purpose and every decision is behind the typed JSON API, but a client-side regression can only be caught by the Playwright suite, not by the type system.

Text / URL / theme edits are browser-visible in ~0.9 s because the editor debounces 250 ms and then reloads the preview document. The engine itself is 137 ms median. This is a UI policy choice, reported rather than optimised away.
The Mobile toggle reproduces the mobile TREE and its CSS layout at 390 CSS px. It does NOT reproduce deviceScaleFactor 3 or hasTouch:true — only the Playwright QA suites do, with real contexts.
ROUTE enablement is not wired. evaluateRouteDisable exists and the Pages rail is the obvious home for it; this phase shipped region enablement only.
A brand (logo) decision is recorded but is NOT visible in the preview: it is applied by the production bake. The panel says so; the operator cannot see the result until a build.
The image inspector takes a server-side file path. There is no upload endpoint, no thumbnail browser and no media library — out of scope by contract.

svg-text bindings are schema-supported but UNEXERCISED: the linear.app template has 0 of 9,929. Any claim about that path on this fixture would be unfounded; the domainchecker.co.kr / stripe.com lineages are where those cases live.

Site switching re-opens a full runtime (slots + bindings + preview). For a site on a DIFFERENT template that costs a cold materialize (~3.2 s); for a site on the same template it reuses the warm preview workspace.

The editor scans page-regions runs by templateId and takes the newest match. A project whose region compile predates a template recompile simply has no region panel — reported as unavailable, never approximated.

The geometry-zero result is measured on ONE template. It is structural (outline never participates in layout; no node or attribute is added to the customer subtree) and the failure mode a border-based technique produces was measured too — but 'exactly 0' is a statement about linear.app's 8,010-element document at two viewports, not a proof for every site.
